newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PRESIDENT APPOINTS NEW MINISTERS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PRESIDENT APPOINTS NEW MINISTERS.

text.p: Poland's president on Friday appointed heads of two key portfolios, to be created on January 1 under a cabinet reorganisation, confirming the liberal former privatisation chief Wieslaw Kaczmarek as economy minister.
Leszek Miller, so far the cabinet chief-of-staff, was appointed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski as the powerful minister of the interior and administration, PAP news agency reported.
The two ministries are being set up under a sweeping reform of the government, launched in October and aimed at streamlining decision-making.
They fell to politicians from the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), the bigger of the two groups in the leftist government, as envisaged in an earlier coalition deal.

The deal gave the coalition's junior partner, the Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the treasury portfolio, which replaced the less powerful privatisation ministry in October and was put in charge of supervising and selling all state assets.
Kaczmarek -- who as privatisation minister proved one of the most pro-reform SLD members -- will now be in charge of devising industrial and foreign trade policies.
He has been deputy treasury minister since his former portfolio was abolished.
The cabinet reorganisation, due to last for several more months, provides for creating several new ministries, merging some and liquidating others.

Kwasniewski also appointed the current interior minister Zbigniew Siemiatkowski as a cabinet minister without portfolio. Siemiatkowski, an SLD member, will be in charge of the security service. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
